variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: FlashAttention is an IO-aware way to compute dense, exact scaled dot-product attention without writing the full attention matrix to slow accelerator memory. It tiles queries, keys, and values into fast on-chip memory, maintains numerically stable softmax statistics, and writes compact results back to high-bandwidth memory (HBM).
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Q, K, and V
pairs.detail: Queries have shape B x Hq x N x d.
pairs.explanation: Queries have shape B x Hq x N x d. Keys and values use B x Hkv x N x d. In standard multi-head attention Hq = Hkv; grouped-query attention can use fewer KV heads.

pairs.label: Scores and probabilities
pairs.detail: S = QK^T / sqrt(d) and P = softmax(S) each have shape B x Hq x N x N when materialized.
pairs.explanation: S = QK^T / sqrt(d) and P = softmax(S) each have shape B x Hq x N x N when materialized. These tensors create the familiar quadratic activation pressure.

pairs.label: Output and row statistics
pairs.detail: O = PV has shape B x Hq x N x d.
pairs.explanation: O = PV has shape B x Hq x N x d. A tiled algorithm carries a running row maximum and normalization term so independently processed blocks combine into the same softmax result.

pairs.label: KV cache
pairs.detail: Serving stores keys and values across layers.
pairs.explanation: Serving stores keys and values across layers. Cache storage scales with B x Hkv x N x d x layers; FlashAttention does not remove this separate linear memory term.

pairs.label: Load bounded tiles
pairs.detail: Move blocks of Q, K, and V into SRAM or shared memory sized for the target kernel and head dimension.
pairs.explanation: Move blocks of Q, K, and V into SRAM or shared memory sized for the target kernel and head dimension.

pairs.label: Compute local scores
pairs.explanation: Evaluate a score tile. Dense exact attention still visits the required query-key pairs.

pairs.label: Merge softmax state
pairs.detail: Update the running maximum and normalization sum, rescaling prior partial output when the maximum changes.
pairs.explanation: Update the running maximum and normalization sum, rescaling prior partial output when the maximum changes.

pairs.label: Accumulate and discard
pairs.detail: Apply the local probabilities to V, accumulate O, then discard the score tile instead of materializing the full N by N surface.

pairs.detail: Pin framework, kernel package, compiler, driver, and container versions.
pairs.explanation: Pin framework, kernel package, compiler, driver, and container versions. Store the supported shape and dtype manifest.

pairs.label: Gate with evidence
pairs.detail: Run dispatch probes, output/gradient checks, target-shape benchmarks, and full-step memory tests on each hardware class.

pairs.explanation: Start with bounded traffic. Monitor fallback or rejection counts, OOMs, latency percentiles, throughput, peak memory, and model-quality proxies.

variants.prompt: Which statement best separates FlashAttention from approximate attention?
options: It evaluates the same dense attention formula in an IO-aware tiled order
It randomly deletes most attention scores
It replaces softmax with a linear activation
It guarantees bitwise-identical output on every backend
variants.explanation: FlashAttention is exact at the mathematical-operation level. Tiling and online softmax change execution and floating-point order, not the dense attention rule.
